newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss money rates lower after SNB action.
newsitem.headline: Swiss money rates lower after SNB action.

text.p: Swiss money market rates eased after the Swiss National Bank (SNB) was reported to have conducted currency swaps, and added liquidity to the money market.
"The SNB did swaps in the currency market," said one Swiss trader, who added that the action came at around 0700 GMT.
He said the action was somewhat unusual, as the SNB has not been seen in currency markets with swaps recently.
He said the swaps were for four months, taking them past year-end. The swaps were said to have been priced at 137 ticks.
In addition, the SNB also added liqudity to the money market, but the additions were at different rates.
The price was generally seen tending below two percent.
The SNB additions helped bring short rates lower, but traders said the money market anyway appeared to be well supplied with liquidity.
Tomorrow/next money was quoted at 1-3/4 percent, but traders noted that tomorrow/next money was something of a technical misnomer, given the long weekend in the U.S.
The operations helped to push the mark/Swiss exchange rate to 81.05 centimes from 80.85 centimes this morning, traders said.
